A build-along course

Building Ostinato

A step sequencer, a synthesiser, a gallery, a jam room, an embeddable player and the adapter that deploys it — built from an empty folder, using every part of Svelte 5 and SvelteKit 3 that earns its place, including everything the September and October 2026 releases added. Every feature is used for something, explained from first principles, and tested end to end.

39 chapters Svelte 5.57SvelteKit 3.1.0Vitest 5Web AudioA custom adapter

Everything we'll cover

  1. 01 What we are building Ostinato: a groovebox in the browser — a step sequencer with synthesised drums and bass, shareable patterns, a gallery, live jam rooms and an embeddable player.
  2. 02 One file to configure everything SvelteKit 3 keeps its whole configuration inside the Vite plugin. This chapter reads vite.config.ts top to bottom: what each option does, what it costs, and what was removed since SvelteKit 2.
  3. 03 The map: everything the framework has to offer Every Svelte 5 and SvelteKit 3 feature this project uses, and the file it lives in — including every item from the September and October 2026 releases, up to 3.1.0.
  4. 04 A note is a class One number — the MIDI note — and everything a sequencer needs derived from it. Why it is a class, why it is immutable, and why that combination is exactly what $state wants.
  5. 05 Musical time, in seconds The conversions between steps and seconds — tempo, swing, velocity — kept apart from both the scheduler and the pattern so they can be tested with a calculator.
  6. 06 The pattern Everything the sequencer plays, as plain data — a deliberate choice about what $state can and cannot see — plus the valibot schemas that check a pattern arriving from anywhere.
  7. 07 A pattern in a URL A link is a save. The codec packs a pattern into about two hundred characters of base64url, versioned, with tests for every way a link can be damaged.
  8. 08 Stored patterns and presets The DTO — the pattern as JSON without a Note in it — and three presets written as strings you can read like a drum machine.
  9. 09 The instruments A kick, a snare, a hi-hat, a clap, a bass and a lead, each built from oscillators, noise and a filter at the moment it is needed. No samples, and a recipe you can read.
  10. 10 One step, scheduled The function both players share: given a pattern, a step index and a time, schedule every hit. Sharing it is what makes “the file sounds like the studio” a property rather than a hope.
  11. 11 The engine: where the audio graph meets reactivity One AudioContext, created lazily, a master fader, and a channel strip per track built on first request with getOrInsertComputed. The state getter is the bridge between a browser event and Svelte, built on createSubscriber.
  12. 12 Two clocks: the scheduler The heart of the instrument. Why setInterval cannot keep time, how a look-ahead timer and the audio clock together can, and why the playhead is a third clock.
  13. 13 Render to a file, and load one The same scheduling function through an OfflineAudioContext gives a WAV that sounds like the studio; forty-four bytes of header make it a file every editor opens; and a SvelteMap holds the samples people drop on a track.
  14. 14 The session: a pattern and its history A class in a .svelte.ts file holds the pattern as deep $state, keeps undo as snapshots, autosaves with a root effect, and can be tested without a component.
  15. 15 A knob A control the web does not have: drag, scroll and arrow keys, a $bindable value, a spring on the pointer, $props.id() for the label, and a wheel listener that must not be passive.
  16. 16 Pads and the grid One pad is a button with a class list; the grid is a keyed {#each} with animate:flip, bind:group for the brush, a function binding for the row checkbox, bind:indeterminate, and a contenteditable name.
  17. 17 The transport and the mixer Play, tempo, swing and volume; a strip per track with level, pan, mute, solo and a meter drawn by an attachment at sixty frames a second; and $inspect.trace in the one effect most likely to re-run for the wrong reason.
  18. 18 Panels that are history entries A sheet on a phone, a sidebar on a desktop — one component, one MediaQuery. Opening it is a shallow goto, closing it is the back button: shallow routing.
  19. 19 The studio page A universal load decides where the pattern comes from; the page builds the instrument, provides it through context, restores after hydration, snapshots across navigation, and wires the keyboard, the window and the body.
  20. 20 Sound in, patterns out The sound panel: bind:files, a DataTransfer to clear it, a waveform drawn by an attachment factory. The share panel: a link, a WAV rendered speculatively with fork, $effect.pending(), media bindings, and a form with preflight validation.
  21. 21 The schema, and the environment Four tables in Drizzle, a pattern as one JSON column, relations for the query builder, one libSQL client with WAL, and every environment variable declared once with a valibot schema.
  22. 22 Identity without passwords A signed cookie says which handle this browser is. HMAC-SHA256 with crypto.subtle, one null for every failure, getRequestEvent() inside helpers, and a shared handle schema that the server enforces and the form preflights.
  23. 23 Reads: query, batch and prerender The store returns Published records with real patterns inside; the .remote.ts file turns them into query, query.batch for thirty cards in one request, and prerender for the featured strip computed at build time.
  24. 24 Writes: command and form Commands with single-flight refreshes, a publish form that works with JavaScript off, invalid(issue.handle(...)) for a 409 under the right field, two submit buttons, a redirect from a form handler, a per-card delete form with remove.for(id), and what the browser is handed when a write is refused.
  25. 25 A live query: the jam room One pattern many browsers edit. An in-memory broadcaster, query.live as an async generator with finally for leaving, a one-value mailbox so slow browsers get the latest, and commands that refresh nothing because the stream already did.
  26. 26 Hooks: around every request handle as a sequence — identity, then security with a font preload filter; handleFetch, and why the catch-all needs nothing special from it; handleError by kind; init; and the two universal hooks, transport and reroute.
  27. 27 Two layouts and a group A root layout with view transitions and a progress bar; an (app) group layout with the header, $state.eager for the current link, the new-version banner, and the artist’s name from a remote query; plus the small pieces every page uses.
  28. 28 The landing page is a file Prerendered, with a prerender remote function baked in, hydratable for random numbers that must agree with themselves, a GSAP entrance loaded only for people who will see it, and a demo grid that plays in pure CSS.
  29. 29 The pattern page and its share card params as a typed prop from PageProps, a card address from resolve() with the layout group in the route id, an optimistic love count with withOverride, a Player that provides a studio only if none exists, and a share card rendered by svelte/server with a CSP built from the hashes it returns.
  30. 30 The gallery The sort lives in the URL; await in an {#each} with batched counts; a preview that opens with preloadData and a shallow goto without leaving, in a native modal <dialog>; crossfade between a card and the dialog; and a delete form per card with remove.for(id) and an optimistic override.
  31. 31 The jam room A load that makes a missing room a real 404, params as a typed prop, and the live query on screen: $derived(await room) so the page follows every yield, overridable {let} deriveds for knobs in mid-gesture, room.connected and reconnect(), online from the window, presence with animate:flip, a handle form that carries the room id, and every edit as a command — with the server’s reason when one is refused.
  32. 32 Diagnostics, tracing and the API An in-memory span exporter and the instrumentation file that registers it; a page that reads the adapter’s virtual module, event.platform, updated.check() and $state.snapshot; and three endpoints — the resolver the reroute hook asks, a QUERY search with a co-located test, and the plain JSON the embed fetches.
  33. 33 A custom element, built twice <ostinato-player>: compiled as a custom element for one folder only through dynamicCompileOptions, and again as one standalone file by a second Vite config. $host() for events, extend for methods that exist before the component mounts, document.currentScript for where it came from.
  34. 34 An adapter, from scratch What an adapter is: writeClient, writePrerendered, generateServerInstance per function, a runtime bundled with rolldown, an instrumentation initialiser and builder.instrument, an emulate() for development, and adapter-provided Vite plugins. Then the part that is only this adapter: a catch-all with no routes, and applyReroute.
  35. 35 The service worker The application shell cached on install from $app/manifest, resolved with $app/paths, versioned by version from $app/env, typed through $app/service-worker and its own tsconfig in src/service-worker/ — and the two paths it must never cache, with the reason.
  36. 36 The security posture One place for the decisions spread across seven files: a CSP in auto mode with the three directives this app needs, CSRF with an empty trusted list, the signed cookie’s flags, one set of security headers for what SvelteKit renders and what the adapter serves as files, CORS on exactly one endpoint, a test that proves the policy covers every inline script, one that proves it blocks nothing else, and one that proves the prerendered page is not left out.
  37. 37 Unit tests, and tests in a real browser Two Vitest projects: pure logic in Node, $state and audio in Chromium. Round-trips for the codec, headers read back with a DataView, a forged cookie, a route partition, and a Session tested with flushSync and no component.
  38. 38 End to end, and what it found Forty-two scenarios on a desktop and a Pixel 7, against node build/index.js on a fresh database — the five real bugs the suite found: a back navigation that never rendered, an await that ran once, an autosave that overwrote the save, a crash in headless Chromium, and a 500 on every vanity address; two a probe found that the suite now pins: a refused edit that said nothing, and delete forms that were never enhanced; and the ones a review found, each with the test that now fails without its fix.
  39. 39 Where next, and the tools that helped The sv add-on that wrote AGENTS.md and the Claude settings, the Svelte MCP server that caught a compile error before the compiler did, #lib imports, the verify script that gates a commit — and five directions the project could go.

Every code block in this course is read out of the finished project in ostinato at build time — file and line numbers included — so it cannot drift from what the code actually says. Type it out rather than pasting where you can: the errors you make and fix are the part that sticks. Where the project made a decision, the chapter says what the alternative was and why it lost.
